quarantined_tests.reason: Rerun-only failure detected across multiple runs
quarantined_tests.fix_commit_notes: Root cause: test_peer_heartbeat_timeout read the wall clock (time.time()) and used time.sleep() margins to judge timeout — a scheduler stall on a loaded CI runner could push elapsed time past or below the timeout boundary, causing a 50% flake rate (issues #776, #778, #779 each caught a re-detection). Fix: MockPeer now accepts an injectable clock parameter (default time.monotonic); tests use FakeClock, a manually-advanced, thread-safe clock that only moves when the test calls clock.advance(). The boundary assertion verifies strict greater-than (>) semantics at exactly the timeout value and one step past it. test_peer_heartbeat_timeout_is_deterministic repeats the scenario 200 times in a single test run, making any residual timing dependency immediately visible. reset_heartbeat sets is_alive=True under the lock to close the bare-attribute-write race on the recovery path. PR #845 merged 2026-11-19; entry retained as a dequarantined audit record with 10 consecutive clean passes. Follow-up (#807, #835, #838, #839): the boundary assertion advanced the FakeClock by 0.3, which is not binary-representable, so (start + 0.3) - start rounded above or below the timeout depending on the start value (e.g. any start in 200..249 gave elapsed > 0.3). The test now uses binary-exact durations (HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT=0.25, HEARTBEAT_STEP=0.125) and test_peer_heartbeat_timeout_boundary_independent_of_clock_start checks the boundary across several clock start values.
